vedicSutras.name: Criss-Cross Multiplication (Urdhva Tiryagbhyam)
steps: Step 1: Multiply unit digits vertically: (Units × Units)
Step 2: Cross multiply outer and inner pairs and add with carry: (Tens × Units + Units × Tens)
Step 3: Multiply tens digits vertically: (Tens × Tens) + carry
vedicSutras.timeSaved: 15 seconds vs standard school long multiplication

vedicSutras.name: Base 100 / 1000 Multiplication (Nikhilam Navatashcaramam)
steps: Step 1: Write deviations from 100: (e.g. 96 is -4, 93 is -7)
Step 2: Right side = Product of deviations: (-4) × (-7) = 28
Step 3: Left side = Cross add either number with other's deviation: (96 - 7) = 89
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Deviations: +6 and +8. Right side: 6 × 8 = 48. Left side: 106 + 8 = 114. Combine: 11448 in 3 seconds!

vedicSutras.name: Squaring Numbers Ending in 5 (Ekadhikena Purvena)
steps: Step 1: Last two digits are ALWAYS 25 (since 5² = 25)
Step 2: Multiply the preceding number (n) by its successor (n + 1)
vedicSutras.walkthrough: Preceding number = 7. Next integer = 8. 7 × 8 = 56. Tack on 25 ⇒ 5625 in 2 seconds!

vedicSutras.name: Multiply Any Number by 11
steps: Write the first digit on the far left and the last digit on the far right
Add adjacent pairs of digits from right to left, carrying over 1 if sum ≥ 10

vedicSutras.name: Multiplying & Dividing by 25 and 125
steps: To multiply by 25: Divide by 4, then multiply by 100 (add 00)
To divide by 25: Multiply by 4, then divide by 100
To multiply by 125: Divide by 8, then multiply by 1000 (add 000)

shortcuts.title: Fraction ↔ Percentage Table Conversion
shortcuts.normalMethod: Multiply by x/100 and do long division with decimals.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Substitute equivalent memorized fraction (e.g. 37.5% = 3/8) and cancel directly with the base number.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Fractions cancel into whole numbers instantly, avoiding multi-decimal floating point calculations.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Confusing 1/9 (11.11%) with 1/11 (9.09%). Tip: Denominator 9 produces repeated 11s; denominator 11 produces repeated 09s!

shortcuts.title: Quadratic Sign-Flip 5-Second Rule
shortcuts.normalMethod: Factorize both equations into roots, solve both, and compare all 4 pairs.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Inspect equation signs first: If signs are (-, +) roots are (+, +). If (+, +) roots are (-, -). If both constants are negative, choose CND immediately!
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Roots of a quadratic with negative constant term have opposite signs (+ and -). Two equations each having one positive and one negative root overlap, making a strict inequality impossible.
shortcuts.normalSteps: Calculate roots for x (+17, -3) and roots for y (+21, -2), then cross-compare (17 vs 21, 17 vs -2, -3 vs 21, -3 vs -2). Takes 45s.
shortcuts.topperSteps: Both c < 0 (constant terms -51 and -42 are negative). Mark 'CND / No relation' immediately in 3 seconds!
shortcuts.commonMistake: Forgetting that leading coefficients (a and d) must be divided out when roots are calculated.

shortcuts.title: Alligation Cross Method for Weighted Mixtures
shortcuts.normalMethod: Set up algebraic equations with x and y: c₁x + c₂y = cₘ(x + y) and solve.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Place cheaper (C) and dearer (D) at top corners, mean (M) at center. Cross difference gives the exact ratio: (D - M) : (M - C).
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Conservation of total value: x(M - C) = y(D - M).
shortcuts.example: Mix tea at ₹60/kg and ₹85/kg to get average of ₹75/kg.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Mixing Cost Price with Selling Price. If one value has profit, convert it to pure Cost Price first!

shortcuts.title: 2-Year and 3-Year CI-SI Difference Formula
shortcuts.normalMethod: Calculate 2 years SI = 2PR/100, calculate 2 years CI = P(1+R/100)² - P, then subtract.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Use direct formula: Diff₂ = P × (R/100)² for 2 years. Diff₃ = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100) for 3 years.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: The second year interest difference is purely the simple interest earned on the first year's interest: (PR/100) × (R/100).
shortcuts.example: Diff between CI and SI on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 12% p.a.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Using this 2-year formula when compounding is half-yearly (which converts 2 years into 4 compounding cycles).

shortcuts.title: LCM Work Efficiency Method
shortcuts.normalMethod: Add fractions: 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20, find common denominator, invert at the end.
shortcuts.topperMethod: Set total work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units. Efficiency of A = 5 u/d, B = 4 u/d, C = 3 u/d. Total = 12 u/d. Days = 60 / 12 = 5 days.
shortcuts.whyItWorks: Integer efficiency units avoid fractions entirely, eliminating fraction addition mistakes.
shortcuts.example: A in 12 days, B in 18 days. Both together?
shortcuts.topperSteps: Work = 36 units. A = 3, B = 2. Combined = 5. Days = 36/5 = 7.2 days in 6s.
shortcuts.commonMistake: Forgetting to subtract negative efficiency of emptying pipes.
